subject: Supply Chain & Logistics
title: Upstream vs. Downstream
description: A micro-lesson that makes Upstream vs. Downstream usable.

hook.text: A cotton farmer in India and a shopper in New York are both part of the same chain. Who is upstream?

buildup.text: Upstream means toward raw materials—farms, mines, and component makers. Closer to the source.

discovery.text: Downstream means toward the customer—distributors, retailers, and delivery. Closer to the buyer.

twist.text: Problems upstream ripple downstream fast. A late shipment of fabric delays thousands of jackets.

climax.text: Smart companies manage both directions. They share forecasts up and track demand down.

punchline.text: Upstream builds it. Downstream sells it. Both must sync.

quiz.question: What does 'upstream' mean in a supply chain?
